items.item: Each category in the tree shows a product count, the page states whether counts include subcategories, and in the sample data every parent's total equals its own products plus the totals of its children
items.evidence: Tree 'Products' column renders fmtCount(totalCount(r.id)) for every row. Detail panel dl explicitly distinguishes 'Own products' vs 'Total products' (buildDetailHtml), stating that the latter includes subcategories. Verified against SEED data: Electronics children sum to 546+349+272+0=1167 matching the screenshot's 1,167; Home & kitchen 403+567+95=1065 matches 1,065; Fashion 530+372+333=1235 matches 1,235; Sports & outdoors 118+157+49=324 matches 324; Books & media 412+97+64=573 matches 573.

items.item: The tree exposes its structure to screen readers (role="tree" and "treeitem", or nested lists) with aria-expanded on parent nodes and the selected node marked, and nodes can be expanded, collapsed and selected from the keyboard
items.evidence: Markup uses role="treegrid" on the table, role="row" on <tr> and role="gridcell"/role="columnheader" on cells (page.html lines 55-61, 374-383) — not role="tree"/"treeitem" and not a nested-list structure, so it doesn't match either accepted pattern. aria-expanded and aria-selected are correctly applied on rows and onTreeKey() does implement full keyboard expand/collapse/select (ArrowRight/Left/Enter/Space), but the exposed role model itself fails the stated requirement.

items.item: Searching by name keeps the ancestors of each matching category visible and expanded so its place in the hierarchy is clear, and a search with no matches says so
items.evidence:
visibleRows() builds a 'keep' set that walks up parentId chains for every match and includes them (page.html lines 332-340), and renderTree() forces isExpanded=true for all rows while a query is active. No-match state renders `

No category matches "${q}"

` with a 'Clear search' button (#no-match).

items.item: The detail panel shows the selected category's full path (such as "Home › Kitchen › Cookware"), name, URL slug, parent, visibility status, product count with a link to those products, and the last modified date and user
items.evidence: Breadcrumb (pathTo) and name/slug/status/Activity ('Last changed by X on date') are present in buildDetailHtml. But there is no distinct 'Parent' field, only the breadcrumb implies it. More importantly, `${kids.length ? renderSubcategoriesSection(cat, kids) : renderProductsSection(cat)}` means any category that has children (i.e. every top-level/branch category, as shown in the screenshot) never renders the product list/'View all N products' link at all — only leaf categories get a product-count link, so the required 'product count with a link to those products' is missing for most categories.

items.item: Hidden or inactive categories are marked in the tree with a text label or icon (such as "Hidden"), not only by greying out
items.evidence: Tree rows render a status pill `${cap(r.status)}` using STATUS_TONE, so inactive categories (e.g. 'Outerwear' under Women's clothing, 'Movies & TV', 'Music') show a text label 'Inactive' distinct from the 'Active' green pill, not just dimmed styling.

items.item: Deleting a category that still has products or subcategories is blocked or requires choosing where to move them, and the confirmation names the category and the counts affected
items.evidence: openDeleteConfirm() computes `blocked = total > 0 || kids.length > 0` and when blocked shows `Can't delete "${cat.name}"` with text `${cat.name} has ${N} products and ${M} subcategories. Move or remove them first.` and only a Close button — deletion is fully blocked and the dialog names the category plus both counts.

items.item: A category can be given a new parent without drag-and-drop (a parent picker or "Move to…" action), and the picker excludes the category itself and its own descendants
items.evidence: Context menu has a 'Move to…' item (data-act="move") opening openMoveDialog(), which builds `exclude = new Set([cat.id, ...descendantsOf(cat.id)])` and filters the <select id="f-parent"> options against it, so the category and its own descendants cannot be chosen as the new parent.

items.item: Selecting another category while the detail form has unsaved edits asks to save or discard first
items.evidence: selectCategory() (page.html lines 450-463) has no dirty-check or guard at all. The edit dialog's own dismiss paths — `$('backdrop').addEventListener('click', () => { closeFormDialog(); closeConfirmDialog(); })` and the Escape-key handler — close the form immediately and silently discard any typed changes with no save/discard prompt.

items.item: With nothing selected the detail panel shows a prompt instead of blank fields, a catalogue with no categories offers to create the first one, and the tree has loading and load-error-with-retry states
items.evidence: detail-section's data-state="empty" block shows 'Select a category to see its details' plus an 'Add category' button; tree-panel's data-state="empty" block shows 'No categories yet' / 'Create your first category to start organizing products.' with a `#tree-empty-add` button; both regions also define data-state="loading" (skeleton rows / aria-busy) and data-state="error" (role="alert" with a Retry button wired to `#tree-retry`/`#detail-retry`), all reachable via the `?state=empty|loading|error` URL param handled in boot().

notes: No template tells from the listed set were observed: no greeting header, no KPI icon tiles, no gradients/glass/backdrop-blur, no emoji icons (the overflow button uses a plain '⋮' Unicode glyph, not an emoji), no rainbow multi-color status (just two tones: green/active and slate/inactive), no sidebar promo card, no decorative chart, no hover-lift (only background-color hover states), no oversized radius (audit reports radii:[4]; dialogs use standard rounded-lg/rounded-md), and no navy-sidebar/indigo-accent theme (sidebar is bg-slate-50 with a plain blue accent). The UI reads as a plausible, utilitarian internal admin tool rather than an AI-dashboard pastiche. Main substantive gaps are the detail panel's missing product link for parent categories (item 4), the treegrid-vs-tree/treeitem ARIA pattern mismatch (item 2), and the complete absence of an unsaved-changes guard (item 8).
